content.comment_body: Hello, I have an older [product_name] [article_no] module connected to KNX, and after installing solar panels last year, the installation company also included a digital meter (NZR WSD 32, see [url]). I am inexperienced with electronics, but I want to know if I can connect the S0-Pulse output DIN 43864 of the meter to the inputs of the [product_name] module and measure the energy produced. How should I proceed? I have a CAT6 UTP cable prepared between the [product_name] and the meter. I believe one pair would be enough to connect them, but which wires should be connected? Many thanks for the help.

If you want to use the S0 interface of the NZR WSD 32, you will need fast counter capability. This is not available on the KNX module but is present on the [product_name] base module (inputs I5 and I6). You can process signals up to 1 kHz on those inputs. In your program, you can use a trigger threshold (see the application example on the [company_name] website) or count the pulses using an up/down counter. Here's an example: [url]
Thanks for your advice. How should I make the physical connection? Will the 27V from the WSD be too high for the [product_name] module?
Hi, you can find this information in the [product_name] manual. A [product_name] 12/24 module accepts up to 28.8V as its power supply and at its inputs.

Connect + from your 24V power source to terminal 41 of the meter. Connect terminal 40 of the meter to a digital input of your [product_name] module. That should be sufficient! However, regular digital inputs might be too slow to count pulses; the impulse duration is 50 ms, and the minimum required is approximately 250 ms. Therefore, you need to use a high-speed input on the [product_name] module.
